([[Laurinburg, North Carolina]]) | college = *[[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2005–2007) *[[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]] (2008–2010) | draft_year = 2010 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 51 | draft_team = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | career_start = 2010 | career_end = 2017 | career_number = | career_position = [[Power forward]] / [[Center (basketball)|center]] | years1 = 2010–2011 | team1 = [[Maine Red Claws]] | years2 = 2012–2014 | team2 = [[Mitsubishi Diamond Dolphins]] | years3 = 2014–2015 | team3 = [[Bnei Herzliya]] | years4 = 2015 | team4 = [[Indios de Mayagüez]] | years5 = 2015 | team5 = [[Yulon Dinos]] | years6 =2016 | team6 =[[Passlab Yamagata Wyverns]] | years7 = 2016–2017 | team7 = Nakhon Pathom Mad Goat | highlights = *Second-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] (2010) *WAC All-Newcomer Team (2009) *2× WAC All-Defensive Team (2009, 2010) | HOF_player = | medaltemplates ={{Medal|Sport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{Medal|Country|{{flagu|Bahamas}}}} {{Medal|Competition|[[FIBA CBC Championship]]}} {{Medal|Gold|[[2014 FIBA CBC Championship|2014 Tortola]]| [[Bahamas national basketball team|Bahamas]]}} }} '''Magnum Rolle''' (born February 23, 1986) is a Bahamian former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the Nakhon Pathom Mad Goat of the [[Thailand Basketball League]]. Born in [[Freeport, Bahamas]], Rolle did not play basketball until his freshman year of high school and was taught by his coach at St. George's High School, Darrel Sears. After his senior year at St. George's, Rolle transferred to the [[Laurinburg Institute]] in North Carolina, where he was an integral part in leading the team to an undefeated record and the national prep school championship. He was considered a five-star prospect out of Laurinburg, and committed to play at [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU). Rolle came off the bench on a team that reached the [[Final Four]] in his freshman campaign. After his [[Sophomore year|sophomore]] year, he transferred to [[Louisiana Tech University|Louisiana Tech]] in 2007 and was forced to skip the [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08 season]] as a [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]. While a [[Junior (education year)|junior]], Rolle tripled his points-per-game average from 4.0 to 12.2. He was named to the All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] (Western Athletic Conference) Defensive Team and All-WAC Newcomer Team. In his [[senior (education)|senior]] year, he led the WAC in [[block (basketball)|block]]s and finished fourth in career blocked shots at Louisiana Tech despite playing only two seasons. He was drafted with the 51st overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and was subsequently traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Rolle was waived by the Pacers on October 25, at the end of training camp and was later chosen with the third overall pick in [[2010 NBA Development League Draft]] by the [[Maine Red Claws]]. ==Early life== Rolle was born on February 23, 1986, in [[Freeport, Bahamas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=185995|title=Magnum Rolle Bio|work=[[LSU Tigers]]|publisher=[[Louisiana State University]]|access-date=June 28, 2010|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222754/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=185995|url-status=dead}} His mother is Maryse Rolle, a painter, and he has one sibling.{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Lewis|url=http://www.tribune242.com/sports/07152010_MagnumCelebrated_sports|title=Ministers congratulate Magnum Rolle on NBA achievement|work=Bahamas Information Services|publisher=[[The Bahamas Tribune]]|date=July 15, 2010|access-date=July 21, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717101112/http://www.tribune242.com/sports/07152010_MagnumCelebrated_sports|archive-date=2011-07-17|url-status=dead}} He was named after [[Tom Selleck]]'s TV show ''[[Magnum, P.I.]]''{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Dufresne|author2=Robyn Norwood |author3=Diane Pucin |author4=Steve Springer |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-apr-01-sp-finalnotes1-story.html|title=Hollins Is Hurt but Will Play|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|page=D10|date=April 1, 2006|access-date=June 28, 2010}} He can trace his ancestry to freed slaves and is a distant cousin of [[National Football League]] (NFL) players [[Myron Rolle|Myron]], [[Antrel Rolle|Antrel]], and [[Samari Rolle]].{{cite magazine|first=S.L.|last=Price|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1114456/index.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091021080219/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1114456/index.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 21, 2009|title=Rolle Call|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Time Inc.]]|date=December 10, 2007|access-date=June 29, 2010}} Originally a [[association football|soccer]] player, Rolle did not play basketball until he was 15, when local coach Darrel Sears saw him walking across a basketball court and saw Rolle's great height. Sears asked if he knew how to play; Rolle said no. Sears asked him to try shooting from the foul line. His first shot, according to Rolle, completely missed the backboard and fell into the bushes behind it. At the time Rolle was not interested in the game and only attended Sears' practices because free fried chicken was provided.{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Coakley|url=http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/359898352218658.php|title=Magnum Drafted in NBA|work=[[The Freeport News]]|date=June 26, 2010|access-date=June 29, 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100629104058/http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/359898352218658.php|archive-date=June 29, 2010}} ==High school and prep school career== At St. George's High School in Freeport, Rolle quickly developed his basketball skills and also competed in [[track and field]] events. He averaged 20.3 points and 13.6 [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s per game while enrolled at that school. Rolle first dreamed of playing in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) when he was 16 years old, after he came back from a basketball camp in [[Arkansas]], but had some academic issues to work out. Rolle's [[grade point average]] (GPA) was 1.0 early in his career at St. George's, forcing him to repeat ninth grade. Due to a drive to succeed academically and athletically, he eventually raised his GPA to 3.0.{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Coakley|url=http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/313280423310184.php|title=When destiny and fate cross paths|work=[[The Freeport News]]|date=March 18, 2010|access-date=June 30, 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100702025927/http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/313280423310184.php|archive-date=July 2, 2010}} In 2003, following his senior year at St. George's, Rolle attended the Nike All-America Camp and convinced his mother to let him attend a [[university-preparatory school|preparatory school]] in the United States, where he could showcase his abilities and hone his talents.{{cite news|url=http://www.puertorico-herald.org/issues/2003/vol7n38/NikeCamp-en.html|title=Nike Camp Gets International Flavor|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[Puerto Rico Herald]]|date=July 7, 2003|access-date=June 28, 2010}} They eventually settled on the [[Laurinburg Institute]], a small school in North Carolina founded in 1904. Due to an unrepaired leak, the school's gymnasium was condemned in 1997, and the basketball team was forced to play home games as far as {{convert|30|mi|km}} away.{{cite news|url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/12098742/|title=Tiny prep school well represented at NCAAs|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[MSNBC]]|date=April 1, 2006|access-date=June 30, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101225035131/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/12098742|archive-date=December 25, 2010|url-status=dead}} In Rolle's only year at the institute, his team went 40–0 and won the national prep school championship. Under head coach Chris Chaney, Rolle recorded a per-game average of 10.1 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 4.5 blocked shots and had a [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]] and [[free throw]] percentage of 64 percent and 76 percent, respectively. Rolle also played with the Arkansas Wings on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit while at the Laurinburg Institute. He received scholarship offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. After verbally committing to Florida State in March 2004,{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1166377|title=Magnum Rolle Profile |work=[[Scout.com]]|publisher=[[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]]|access-date=June 30, 2010}} Rolle reopened his recruitment in July.{{cite web|first=Brad|last=Allis|url=http://arizona.scout.com/a.z?s=106&p=2&c=277437&ssf=1&RequestedURL=http%3a%2f%2farizona.scout.com%2f2%2f277437.html|title=Big man is wide open |work=[[Scout.com]]|publisher=[[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]]|date=July 26, 2004|access-date=June 30, 2010}} He decided on LSU, to which fellow Laurinburg teammate Chris Johnson had already committed, and signed his [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] on November 18, 2004. Rolle was listed as the eighth-best [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in the class of 2005 and 32nd overall recruit by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite news|url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=356747|title=Rolle's signature finishes LSU's class|work=[[Rivals.com]]|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=November 18, 2004|access-date=June 30, 2010}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2005}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Magnum Rolle | position = [[Power forward]] | hometown = Freeport, Bahamas | highschool = [[Laurinburg Institute|Laurinburg]] (NC) | feet = 6 | inches = 9 | weight = 209 | 40 = | commitdate = 09/08/2004 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2005 | rivals ref title = LSU Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2005 LSU Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = lsu | scout s = 573 | espn schoolid = 2305 | scout overall = 7 (PF) | rivals overall = 32, 8 (PF) | access-date = July 1, 2010 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===LSU=== {{multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = | header_background = | footer = At LSU, Rolle played alongside [[Tyrus Thomas]] and [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen "Big Baby" Davis]]. | footer_align = left | footer_background = | width = | image1 = Tyrus Thomas.jpg | width1 = 100 | alt1 = Tyrus Thomas | caption1 = | image2 = Glen-davis-warm-up.jpg | width2 = 115 | alt2 = Glen Davis | caption2 = }} ====Freshman==== On November 18, 2005, in an 84–56 defeat of [[Southern Jaguars|Southern University]], Rolle made his collegiate debut, playing 14 minutes and scoring six points while also grabbing three rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=253220099|title=Southern University Jaguars vs. LSU Tigers – Box Score|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 18, 2005|access-date=July 1, 2010}} Rolle shot 4-of-8 from the field and contributed season bests in rebounds (10) and points (8) to help lead LSU past [[Nicholls State University|Nicholls State]]. He equaled his season high in points against the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] on February 2, 2006, in only nine minutes of playing time. The Tigers surprised many with a [[Final Four]] run, and in that game Rolle led the team in rebounds with eight, recorded two points from 1-of-1 shooting, and blocked a shot, all in 14 minutes of playing time. Despite this performance, LSU's opponent [[2005–06 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] ultimately prevailed, 59–45.{{cite news|first=Fred|last=Sturrup|url=http://www.jonesbahamas.com/?c=123&a=8304|title=Magnum Rolle Comes Of Age!|work=[[The Bahama Journal]]|date=April 3, 2006|access-date=July 1, 2010}} During the [[2005-06 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2005–06 season]], Rolle averaged 2.2 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 8.7 minutes per game as a freshman, picking up 21 blocks on the year. ====Sophomore==== Coming into the [[2006-07 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2006–07 season]], the Tigers returned four starters, including [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen "Big Baby" Davis]], and LSU fans hoped that Rolle would replace the shot blocking skills of [[Tyrus Thomas]], who had left early for the NBA. As such, [[Andy Katz]] of ESPN named them the fifth best team in the nation in the preseason.{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Katz|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2491073|title=ESPN.com 2006–07 June Top 25 (1–10)|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=June 19, 2006|access-date=July 1, 2010}} Rolle's averages improved slightly to 4.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 16.7 minutes per contest, with nine starts and 31 blocks. He had a season-best nine rebounds against [[Tulane Green Wave|Tulane]] on December 22, and recorded his first double-digit scoring night against the [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] on March 8, 2007, in the [[2007 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], when he shot 5-for-7 from the field in 18 minutes for 10 points. However, two [[herniated disc]]s in his back impeded further progress.{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Kleinpeter|url=http://www.nola.com/sports/t-p/index.ssf?/base/sports-27/1166856581244330.xml&coll=1|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120630154840/http://www.nola.com/sports/t-p/index.ssf?/base/sports-27/1166856581244330.xml&coll=1|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2012|title=Brady calls for more frontcourt production|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|date=December 23, 2006|access-date=July 2, 2010}} The Tigers finished the year 17–15 and 5–11 in SEC play.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3237084|title=Brady fired as LSU basketball coach|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=February 8, 2008|access-date=July 23, 2010}} Rolle left the LSU program on May 23. LSU coach [[John Brady (basketball)|John Brady]] claimed this was due to concerns over Rolle's development.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2007-05-23-3248855651_x.htm|title=Magnum Rolle leaves LSU|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=May 23, 2007|access-date=July 23, 2010}} Darrel Sears, his former high school coach, said Rolle had been unhappy with LSU since December 2006, and that Brady had been making snide comments about Rolle for a while. After Rolle left LSU, he was courted by Division I schools [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]], [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]], [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]], [[University of Delaware|Delaware]], [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]], and [[South Florida Bulls|South Florida]]. Although initially interested in South Florida due to its proximity to his Bahamas home,{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Coakley|url=http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/289076362910115.php|title=Coach Sears blasts back at Brady of LSU|work=[[The Freeport News]]|date=June 8, 2007|access-date=July 31, 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721162221/http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/289076362910115.php|archive-date=July 21, 2011}} Rolle chose to transfer to Louisiana Tech to play under [[Kerry Rupp]].{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Kleinpeter|url=http://www.nola.com/sports/t-p/index.ssf?/base/sports-31/1181887054144120.xml&coll=1|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120630154850/http://www.nola.com/sports/t-p/index.ssf?/base/sports-31/1181887054144120.xml&coll=1|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2012|title=Former Tigers headed to Tech|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|date=June 15, 2007|access-date=July 31, 2010}} ===Louisiana Tech=== ====Junior==== Rolle was forced to [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] the [[2007-08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08 season]] due to transfer rules. In his first game as a [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Bulldog]], on November 15, 2008, he registered nine rebounds and eight points, including four consecutive points within the last minute, to propel Louisiana Tech past [[Louisiana-Lafayette]], 61–59.{{cite news|first=Barbara|last=Walkin|url=http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/293378236245292.php|title=Magnum returns to basketball in dramatic fashion|work=[[The Freeport News]]|date=November 20, 2008|access-date=July 31, 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721162228/http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/293378236245292.php|archive-date=July 21, 2011}} Rolle's first [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]] came against [[Grambling State]] on November 18, with 12 points and 14 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/magnum_rolle_2010.html|title=Pacers: Prospect Profile 2010: Magnum Rolle|work=[[NBA]]|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive|access-date=June 28, 2010}} He led the team in scoring with a then-career high of 17 points in a [[blowout (sports)|blowout]] 78–55 loss to #10 [[2008-09 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] on December 28, while also contributing seven rebounds.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283630026|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120630154838/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283630026|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2012|title=No. 10 UCLA too much for Louisiana Tech|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=December 28, 2008|access-date=July 23, 2010}} On January 29, 2009, Rolle had a perfect night from the field, shooting 11-for-11 with 23 points. In a 60–52 defeat at the hands of [[Utah State]] on February 7, Rolle fell and injured his hip early in the game, but he came back later to finish with eight points.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290380328|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213181059/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290380328|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 13, 2009|title=Utah State holds off Louisiana Tech for victory|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=February 7, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010}} He had a season high 25 points to go along with 11 rebounds and four blocked shots in leading the Bulldogs to a victory over [[Murray State]] 69–60 on February 21.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290530093|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105092940/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290530093|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 5, 2012|title=Louisiana Tech 69, Murray St. 60|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=February 21, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010}} In the next game, an 80–71 win over [[New Mexico State]], Rolle equalled his season high in points (25) and grabbed 12 rebounds.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290572348|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120630154857/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290572348|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2012|title=Louisiana Tech 80, New Mexico St. 71|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=February 26, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010}} During the [[2008-09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09 season]], Rolle started 30 games for the Bulldogs and averaged 12.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.7 blocks per game. He registered five double-doubles while scoring in excess of 10 points on 18 occasions. After the season, Rolle was named to the All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] Defensive Team and All-WAC Newcomer Team. In addition, the Louisiana Sports Writers Association recognized Rolle as a member of the All-Louisiana third team. Louisiana Tech teammate Kyle Gibson was named to its first team.{{cite web|url=http://www.latechsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041209aaa.html|title=Gibson and Rolle Named All-LSWA|work=[[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]]|publisher=[[Louisiana Tech University]]|date=April 12, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010|archive-date=July 13, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713190215/http://www.latechsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041209aaa.html|url-status=dead}} Rolle briefly flirted with the [[2009 NBA draft]]. He declared for early entry in the draft, but did not hire an [[sports agent|agent]].{{cite news|title=New Mexico State shooting guard Jonathan Gibson declares early entry for NBA draft|work=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]]|publisher=MediaNews Group|date=May 1, 2009}} After talking to NBA spokespeople, who said he was a borderline second-round selection, Rolle considered staying in college an extra year to earn a degree. He eventually pulled his name out of the draft, thus ensuring his college eligibility. ====Senior==== The WAC preseason polls were released on October 29, and Louisiana Tech was predicted to finish sixth in the media poll{{cite web|url=http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817314|title=WAC Men's Basketball Preseason Media Picks Announced|work=[[Western Athletic Conference]]|date=October 29, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225130930/http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817314|archive-date=February 25, 2012|url-status=dead}} and fifth in the coaches poll. Fellow senior Gibson was named to the preseason All-WAC second team, but Rolle was not honored by any preseason award.{{cite web|url=http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817383|title=WAC Announces Men's Basketball Coaches Preseason Picks|work=[[Western Athletic Conference]]|date=October 29, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225130937/http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817383|archive-date=February 25, 2012|url-status=dead}} In the Bulldogs' home opener against [[Arkansas-Little Rock]], Rolle was the leader in scoring with 23 points in crushing the Trojans 86–66. Gibson and [[Olu Ashaolu]] also scored more than 20 points to push Louisiana Tech to a 4–1 start, their best since 2001.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293292348|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091228183235/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293292348|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 28, 2009|title=Louisiana Tech 86, Ark.-Little Rock 66|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 25, 2009|access-date=August 2, 2010}} Rolle's career high in points was 29, scored against [[University of Houston|Houston]] in a 99–94 defeat of the Cougars on December 29; Rolle also grabbed 10 [[rebound (basketball)|board]]s.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293640248|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100226072914/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293640248|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 26, 2010|title=Louisiana Tech 99, Houston 94|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=December 29, 2009|access-date=August 3, 2010}} In the semifinal of the [[2010 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]], against the #1 seeded [[Utah State Aggies]], Rolle injured his ankle less than three minutes into the game, a factor in the Bulldogs' 30-point loss. They finished the regular season 23–10, including a 9–7 record in conference.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300710328|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110225051941/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300710328|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 25, 2011|title=Utah St. 85, Louisiana Tech 55|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 12, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010}} That was good enough for an invitation to the [[2010 CollegeInsider.com Tournament]] (CIT), in which Louisiana Tech defeated [[Southern Miss]] in the first round despite missing Rolle.{{cite web|url=http://www.collegeinsider.com/tournament/2010_game8.html|title=Louisiana Tech Beats Southern Miss|work=CollegeInsider.com|date=March 18, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010}} In Rolle's final collegiate game, he contributed nine points off the bench despite a 69–40 rout of the Bulldogs by [[Missouri State]] in the CIT's quarterfinals.{{cite web|url=http://www.collegeinsider.com/tournament/2010_game11.html|title=Missouri State runs past Louisiana Tech|work=CollegeInsider.com|date=March 22, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010}} During the [[2009-10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10 season]], Rolle started 33 games, in 24 of which he scored in double figures and in 11 of which he had double-doubles. He rejected more shots than anyone else in the WAC, averaging 2.1 blocks per game, and finished fourth in career blocked shots at Louisiana Tech despite playing there for only two seasons. Rolle also posted averages of 8.4 rebounds per game, third in the WAC (behind [[Luke Babbitt]] of [[University of Nevada-Reno|Nevada]] and Chis Oakes of [[San Jose State]]),{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/stats/leaders/WAC/REBAVG/regularseason/yearly|title=NCAA Basketball Stats – WAC Leaders in Rebounds per game|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=August 3, 2010}} and 13.9 points per game, 12th in the WAC.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/stats/leaders/WAC/PTSAVG/regularseason/yearly|title=NCAA Basketball Stats – WAC Leaders in Points Per Game|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=August 3, 2010}} His field goal percentage was 51.1, tied with Babbitt for third in conference and behind [[Tai Wesley]] of Utah State and Ike Okoye of [[Boise State]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/stats/leaders/WAC/FGPCT/regularseason/yearly|title=NCAA Basketball Stats – WAC Leaders in Field Goal Percentage|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=August 3, 2010}} At the conclusion of the season, Rolle was named to the Lefty Driesell All-America Defensive Team, All-WAC Defensive Team, All-WAC Second Team, and All-Louisiana Second Team. He graduated from Louisiana Tech with a bachelor's degree in [[sociology]] in March 2010, becoming the first person in his family to earn a degree. ==Professional career== ===NBA draft=== Prior to the [[2010 NBA draft]], Rolle hired [[Fletcher Cockrell]] to be his agent.{{cite news|url=http://louisianatech.scout.com/2/980030.html|title=Rolle Taken by Indiana In NBA Draft|work=[[Scout.com]]|publisher=[[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]]|date=June 25, 2010|access-date=June 30, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716020606/http://louisianatech.scout.com/2/980030.html|archive-date=2011-07-16|url-status=dead}} [[ESPN]], NBADraft.net, and DraftExpress.com projected him to be a possible mid-to-late second-round selection. He worked out with the [[Washington Wizards]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], and [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite news|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|url=http://www.tribune242.com/sports/06232010_ROLLE-DRAFT_sport|title=Magnum enters 64th NBA Draft|work=[[The Bahamas Tribune]]|date=June 23, 2010|access-date=August 2, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100801044933/http://www.tribune242.com/sports/06232010_ROLLE-DRAFT_sport|archive-date=2010-08-01|url-status=dead}} Dave-Te' Thomas of [[CBS Sports]] said that Rolle had a good wingspan and was very athletic. He added while larger NBA forwards might push him around, he was an intense player and would not back down if challenged. Thomas compared Rolle to former LSU teammate [[Tyrus Thomas]].{{cite web|first=Dave Te'|last=Thomas |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/stats/leaders/WAC/FGPCT/regularseason/yearly|title=Magnum Rolle, Louisiana Tech, 2010 NBA Draft|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=August 3, 2010}} On June 25, Rolle was chosen with the 51st overall pick by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. His rights were traded to the Pacers for [[Ryan Reid (basketball)|Ryan Reid]], who was the 57th overall pick, along with undisclosed cash considerations.{{cite news|first=Cliff|last=Brunt|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2010-06-25-1239744670_x.htm|title=Pacers acquire Rolle in 2nd round|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=June 25, 2010|access-date=September 6, 2010}} Rolle was the first NBA player drafted out of Louisiana Tech since [[Paul Millsap]] was picked by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 47th pick of the [[2006 NBA draft]]. In addition, he was the first [[Grand Bahama|Grand Bahamian]] selected in the draft. Bahamas Minister of Youth Sports and Culture [[Charles Maynard (Bahamian politician)|Charles Maynard]] and Minister of Works and Transport [[Neko C Grant]] congratulated Rolle on his historic achievement. ===Indiana Pacers=== ====Summer League==== {{quote box |width=350px|align = right |qalign = right |bgcolor = #c6dbf7 |quote = He's been by far the best player by a large margin (in camp). He has dominated everything. He has scored. He has rebounded. He has defended well. He has a surprisingly high basketball IQ. He shoots really well and pursues every offensive rebound.|source = Former Indiana Pacers coach [[Jim O'Brien (basketball, born 1952)|Jim O'Brien]], speaking of Magnum Rolle{{cite news|first=Fred|last=Sturrup|url=http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/65099920161089.php|title=Larry Bird/Magnum Rolle connection|work=[[The Freeport News]]|date=July 21, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723080302/http://freeport.nassauguardian.net/sports/65099920161089.php|archive-date=2010-07-23|url-status=usurped}}}} Rolle played well in the 2010 [[Orlando Summer League]], garnering averages of 28 minutes, 13.4 points, seven rebounds, and two blocked shots per game. On opening day of the summer league, the Pacers beat the [[Orlando Magic]] 86–77 behind Rolle's 13 points, five rebounds, two blocks, and a steal. In the second game, an 80–69 loss to the [[New Jersey Nets]], Rolle scored nine points, brought down three rebounds, and rejected three shots. Against the [[Utah Jazz]], Rolle's 10 points, eight rebounds, and four blocks facilitated an 83–74 Pacers win. The fourth game, which ''[[The Bahamas Tribune]]'' said was the most thrilling of the summer league, featured a 27-point deficit erased by Indiana for a comeback win over the [[Boston Celtics]]. Rolle had a double-double, with 19 points and 11 boards. The Pacers and him wrapped up the Orlando Summer League with a 77–73 defeat by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], in which Rolle posted 16 points, eight rebounds and two blocks.{{cite news|first=Renaldo|last=Dorsett|url=http://www.tribune242.com/sports/07132010_Rolle_Sports|title=Magnum Rolle edges nearer NBA dream|work=[[The Bahamas Tribune]]|date=July 13, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717101329/http://www.tribune242.com/sports/07132010_Rolle_Sports|archive-date=2011-07-17|url-status=dead}} ====Training camp==== Rolle, along with fellow Pacer rookie [[Lance Stephenson]], was named one of the "steals of the draft" by ''[[The Boston Globe]]''.{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Washburn|url=http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/articles/2010/07/25/pacers_banking_on_big_moves_next_summer/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100726080036/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/articles/2010/07/25/pacers_banking_on_big_moves_next_summer/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 26, 2010|title=Pacers banking on big moves next summer|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|publisher=[[The New York Times Company]] |date=July 25, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2010}} Rolle was invited to the Pacers' training camp, where he injured his head, requiring stitches. On September 28, the Pacers announced they had officially signed Rolle to a two-year contract, but his salary was not disclosed.{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Kryger|url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20100930/SPORTS04/9300451/Rush-awaits-decision-on-option|title=Rush awaits decision on option|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=September 30, 2010|access-date=September 30, 2010}} In five preseason games, he averaged 1.8 points per game and 1.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2010-10-25-1691752205_x.htm|title=Indiana Pacers waive rookie forward Magnum Rolle|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=October 25, 2010|access-date=November 2, 2010}} However, he was waived on October 25, at the end of training camp, in order to shrink the roster to NBA-mandated 15 players. The Pacers tried to trade [[Dahntay Jones]] and [[Solomon Jones (basketball)|Solomon Jones]] to keep Rolle, but the trade fell through and the Pacers were reluctant to drop Solomon Jones due to a lack of depth in the [[frontcourt]]. Had he made the roster, Rolle would have earned $510,000, but instead he made $50,000 in a buyout.{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Wells|url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20101025/SPORTS04/101025026/Pacers-release-Magnum-Rolle-regular-season-roster-set|title=Pacers release Magnum Rolle, regular-season roster set|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=October 25, 2010|access-date=October 25, 2010}} ===Maine Red Claws=== In the [[2010 NBA Development League Draft]], held on November 1, Rolle was chosen with the third overall pick by the [[Maine Red Claws]]. The Red Claws were the affiliated team of the [[Boston Celtics]] and the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. According to Red Claws general manager [[Jon Jennings]], several D-League teams thought he had the most upside of anyone on the draft.{{cite news|first=Jenn|last=Menendez|url=http://www.pressherald.com/sports/seeking-the-pick-of-the-pot_2010-11-02.html|title=Maine Red Claws: Seeking the pick of the pot|work=[[The Portland Press-Herald]]|date=November 2, 2010|access-date=November 2, 2010}} On November 26, Rolle was waived by the Red Claws because of a knee injury which was due to keep Rolle out 'indefinitely'. In two games with the Red Claws, Rolle averaged 7.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.5 blocks per game. His rights were retained by the Red Claws.[http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/11/26/maine-red-claws-waive-magnum-rolle-due-to-knee-injury/ Maine Red Claws Waive Magnum Rolle Due to Knee Injury] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101128133014/http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/11/26/maine-red-claws-waive-magnum-rolle-due-to-knee-injury/ |date=2010-11-28 }} FanHouse, November 26, 2010 On March 3, 2011, he returned to the Red Claws. He played 13 more games with the Red Claws before he was called up to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Overall, he averaged 14.1 points and 5.5 rebounds in 25.9 minutes per game with the Red Claws.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/rolle_110411.html Maine's Magnum Rolle Signs With Atlanta Hawks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122091715/http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/rolle_110411.html |date=2012-01-22 }} ===Atlanta Hawks=== On April 11, 2011, Rolle signed with the Atlanta Hawks but did not play a game with Atlanta during the 2010–11 season.[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Rolle_PR_041111.html Atlanta Hawks Sign Magnum Rolle] During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], he signed with [[South Korea]]n team [[Changwon LG Sakers]] but also did not appear in a game with Changwon. After the lockout ended, Rolle returned to the Hawks for the training camp.[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/training_camp_2011_pr.html Atlanta Hawks Re-Sign Jason Collins, Ink Tracy McGrady and Keith Benson] However, he was released before the start of the season. ===Orlando Magic=== In July 2012, Rolle joined the Orlando Magic for the 2012 NBA Summer League.[http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/playerProfiles/profileDisplay.jsp?id=1472 ShamSports.com: Magnum Rolle player profile] ===Japan=== In August 2012, Rolle signed with the Mitsubishi Diamond Dolphins of the [[Japanese Basketball League]] for the 2012–13 season. In 2013, he re-signed with the Dolphins for the 2013–14 season. in just his second year became an NBL Allstar and led his team to the playoffs. Rolle also led the league in scoring in the Emperors Cup tournament, advancing to the final four top teams. ===Thailand=== In June 2016, Rolle signed with MadGoats Basketball Club of the [[Thailand Basketball League]], where he finished as the league's MVP ==Career statistics== ===NCAA=== {| class="wikitable collapsible" width="65%" style="background:transparent" !
